title: The incident: severity, incident commander, communication and the timeline

videos.script: Everything so far has been about noticing. This lesson is about the next hour. The page has arrived, customers are failing to buy, and somebody has to decide what happens now. {{page}} An incident is run, not just fixed. One person commands and does not debug. Others investigate. Someone keeps everybody else informed. {{roles}} The lab stages one. A release of payments goes out, and three minutes later checkouts start failing. You declare it, mark it, and ask the first question of every incident: what changed? {{changed}} You roll back before you understand, because customers are waiting and understanding can wait. {{rollback}} And at the end, you build the timeline from the marks the people and the machines left behind. That timeline is where the postmortem of the next lesson begins. {{timeline}}
